name: Hoover
label: Dischord
lede: Four transplants, three singers and one hour-long album, and the band announced it was done the moment it got home from the tour.

eras.title: Everybody moved here
eras.text: In the early '90s D.C.'s underground was booming and pulling people in from all over. Dischord says Ian MacKaye had met most of Hoover's future members in their hometowns while touring with Fugazi, and ran in the same circles once they landed in D.C.

years.p: [[Joe McRedmond|132df41f-6981-4db5-93cc-47aa88b825c9]], from Harrisburg's Admiral, and Christopher Farrall, from D.C.'s Fine Day, start a band called Victor Deluxe. The original bassist is Geoff Farina.
Fred Erskine, from Nebraska, takes over bass from Geoff Farina. Erskine had started on violin at four and trumpet at eight, and he brings the trumpet along.

q: Would start playing his guitar by himself really loud
years.h: Alex Dunham plays his way in, and the band becomes Hoover
years.p: Alex Dunham, newly arrived from Arizona hardcore band Winds of Change, sits in on Victor Deluxe practices and plays along, loud, until they ask him to join. Now there are three singers, and the band becomes Hoover.

years.h: Live at Decibels, Mechanicsburg PA, December 20, 1992
yt: Live at Decibels, Mechanicsburg PA, December 20, 1992

eras.title: Three voices, half a label
eras.text: Hoover's first single came out as what Dischord calls a Dischord/Hoover Limited half-label release. The sound was already its own: Slint's skeleton, Fugazi's muscle, and three members trading whispers and screams.

years.p: Hoover's first single, cut at Inner Ear. Dischord calls it a Dischord/Hoover Limited half-label release.

years.h: Hoover split a record with Lincoln
years.p: Hoover's Two-Headed Coin shares a record with fellow travelers Lincoln on the Art Monk Construction label.
Return, Private and Dries, the three songs that would later close out the CD reissue of The Lurid Traversal of Route 7.

eras.title: Route 7, then the exit
eras.text: The album arrived in early 1994 and the band quit that spring. AllMusic's Charles Spano argues that late-'90s Fugazi may owe Hoover a debt, rather than the other way around.

years.p: Recorded at WGNS in August 1993 with [[Geoff Turner|591fc466-2668-4524-852d-a6cc5f18cff7]] and Juan Carrera producing: ten songs, nearly an hour. Early on, AllMusic notes, Hoover was wrongly dubbed a Fugazi copycat.
years.xp:
Electrolux and Cuts Like Drugs each run past seven minutes. The record got a better hearing later.

The A.V. Club's Jason Heller later called it one of the decade's singular, eerie post-hardcore albums. AllMusic's Ned Raggett heard Drive Like Jehu in it: aggression amped up, lyrics clipped, vocals screamed.

years.h: Hoover come home from tour and split
years.p: Hoover tours behind the album, gets back to D.C. in April, and announces the split. Dischord dates the band from summer 1992 to spring 1994: under two years.

eras.title: Everyone scatters, the record grows
eras.text: Hoover's members fanned out into a string of new bands in D.C. and Louisville, and the album kept finding people. Every few years Hoover came back to finish something.

years.h: Hoover's members scatter: Crownhate Ruin, June of 44, Regulator Watts
years.p: Joe McRedmond and Fred Erskine form [[The Crownhate Ruin|6c13db70-bd59-44a0-8c6a-eeb0d0c8f40d]]; Erskine then joins Louisville's [[June of 44|56f3de75-2c88-4054-a1df-65c661f4ee0f]]. Alex Dunham starts [[Regulator Watts|5f06481f-d8e3-45b6-954d-753abe05952b]] and later Abilene.
years.xp: The Crownhate Ruin ended after 1995's Until the Eagle Grins. Ex-Hoover members also turned up in HiM and [[Beauty Pill|976b28a1-dd68-4c43-ba08-ba15b58963b2]].

years.h: Hoover: the last four songs, finished in 1997
years.p: Hoover regrouped briefly in 1997 to record the four songs written before the 1994 split. They come out as a self-titled record on Slowdime, distributed by Dischord.

years.h: Hoover back on stage, ten years after the split
years.p: Hoover reunites for shows in the US and Europe, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Dischord reissues The Lurid Traversal of Route 7
years.p: Dischord reissues the album on CD with the three Private 7" songs added, running it to thirteen tracks.
Vulture ranks Electrolux, from The Lurid Traversal of Route 7, No. 86 on its list of the 100 greatest emo songs.
